Kevin Trudeau says most people answer the same way when he asks how much money they want: "more." He pushes back — how much more? "A lot." Still no number.

That vagueness, he says, is the real problem. The first thing anyone serious about wealth has to do is get specific — not "more," but an actual number: $20,000 a month, $50,000, whatever it is for you.

Once you have the number, your job is done. Figuring out how to get there isn't your job at all — that part, he says, belongs to the universe.

What's the actual number you've been avoiding naming?

#kevintrudeau #moneymindset #wealthmindset #manifestation #goalsetting #successmindset

Kevin Trudeau was deep into building his Mega Memory courses in the 1980s — loved the work, loved the team — when one question stopped him in his office: what do I really want next?

The answer came out almost embarrassing to say out loud: $200,000 a week, deposited into his account, with no work required. He laughed — the only way he could picture it happening was winning the lottery.

So he said it anyway: "That's not my job, universe. My job is to want it. Your job is to figure out how."

Two weeks later, in a New York deli, the answer sat down right next to him.

What number have you been afraid to say out loud because you don't know how yet?

#kevintrudeau #manifestation #moneymindset #wealthmindset #yourwishisyourcommand #mindset

Kevin Trudeau says there's one question you should be able to answer as fast as your own name: what do you want?

Most people can't. Ask them their address and they rattle it off instantly. Ask what they want and they stall — "let me think about that."

He says that hesitation comes from one habit almost everybody has: trying to figure out HOW before deciding WHAT. How am I going to make that money? How is that even possible? That one habit, he says, is what blocks people from ever reaching the goals and the money they actually want.

Could you answer "what do you want" as fast as your own name?
